hero.caption: A cyan live banner and a peeking next-run card tell the homeowner what the system is doing right now, before they read a word.

hero.title: Place zones on the satellite map
hero.caption: A dock of numbered, color-coded zone badges lets installers drag each valve onto the real property, so zones are recognised by place, not by number.

hero.title: Precision Control forecast sheet
hero.caption: The sheet explains why watering is paused in plain language, with a four-day rain outlook and the exact trigger that fired.

hero.title: Contractor client map with sheet
hero.caption: Name pins with urgent and flag badges sit above a draggable client list, so a contractor can triage a day's route from one screen.

hero.caption: The welcome carousel sells the product with a real ET adjustment chart instead of a generic illustration.

hero.title: Contractor map with live status pins

hero.flag: Sample client names and street addresses appear to be demo data; confirm they are not real customers before publishing.

sequences.title: Controller setup, scan to done
sequences.story: Setting up a controller is the contractor's highest-stakes moment, so the flow runs in short, single-purpose steps with a segmented progress bar. Bluetooth and Wi-Fi trouble is handled with an in-context help sheet rather than a dead end. The flow ends by proving the install works: bulk zone setup, run-all testing, then a confirmation.

frames.title: Connect controller
frames.caption: QR scan sits on top and nearby devices fill in below, so there are two ways in and no manual typing.

frames.title: Having issues? help sheet
frames.caption: Ordered troubleshooting steps and a Contact Support button live in a bottom sheet, so a failed pairing never loses the user's place.

frames.title: Set up zones in bulk
frames.caption: Select-all with a floating action bar applies Map Zones or True ET to 22 zones at once instead of 22 times.

frames.title: System testing
frames.caption: One test runtime, a Test All button and per-zone play controls with status ticks prove the install on the spot.

frames.title: Setup complete
frames.caption: A full progress bar and a celebratory confirmation close the loop and hand the contractor back to the account.
frames.flag: Uses placeholder name 'John Smith's Main Home'.

sequences.title: TRUE ET wizard
sequences.story: TRUE ET replaces a wall of agronomy settings with a guided wizard that asks one plain-language question per screen: hardware, plant type, soil. Every option is a visual card with a 'what this means' explanation, and unknowns fall back to a smart default. The result is a zone profile a non-expert can complete and an expert can still fine-tune.

frames.title: Select zones
frames.caption: The wizard starts by confirming which zones it will configure, with select-all for bulk work.

frames.title: Hardware type
frames.caption: Large icon cards and an 'I'm not sure' default let users answer without knowing the product jargon.

frames.title: Vegetation type
frames.caption: Plant categories are named in everyday language with examples, and an info banner says what the choice changes.

frames.title: Soil type
frames.caption: Soil swatches with a one-line drainage description make a technical input feel like picking a texture.

frames.title: Zone profile complete
frames.caption: A summary of watering days, runtime and cycle-and-soak shows the user what the answers produced, with Advanced Settings one tap away.
frames.flag: Tall frame (1103pt); scrolls beyond one screen.

sequences.title: Map zones and borders
sequences.story: Zones become spatial: the installer pins each valve on a satellite view of the property and draws its coverage outline. The map goes full-bleed, the controls collapse into a bottom bar, and Undo, Reset and Done appear only when relevant. The map then comes back as a thumbnail in zone details so people can recognise a zone by place.

frames.title: Zone details with Map Zone
frames.caption: The zone detail screen offers a Map Zone call-to-action over a satellite preview thumbnail.

frames.title: Place the zone
frames.caption: A one-line hint and a tray of unplaced zone badges teach drag-and-place without a tutorial.

frames.title: Zone selected
frames.caption: The selected badge grows a coverage halo so it is clear which zone is being edited.

frames.title: Draw the border
frames.caption: Undo and Done replace Reset and Edit while drawing, so the toolbar only offers what is useful in the current mode.

frames.title: Zone mapped
frames.caption: The finished outline returns to zone details as a thumbnail with Edit Zone, closing the loop.

sequences.title: Welcome and invite
sequences.story: First launch shows a swipeable carousel that sells value with product visuals: zone mapping, savings and ET tracking. Three clear entry points sit in a docked panel, and 'I received an invite' is a first-class path rather than a buried link. The invite path helps people find the email or text and lands on a confirmed, pre-contextualised account form.

frames.title: Welcome: spatial zone mapping
frames.caption: The first carousel card leads with the map, the most visual part of the product.

frames.title: Welcome: savings on autopilot
frames.caption: A real weekly-summary notification shows the benefit in the place the user will actually see it.

frames.title: Let's find that invite
frames.caption: A friendly sheet routes to Messages or Email in one tap, with 'Request a new invite' as the escape hatch.

frames.title: Welcome, you've been invited
frames.caption: The form opens by naming who invited the user and for which property, so the handover feels trustworthy before any typing.
frames.flag: Placeholder sample data (John Smith / 8123 Main St, Los Angeles 90001 / stock avatar); not a real customer.

system.title: Unified settings components
system.caption: Controller, program and zone settings are built from one set of form components in two variants (C and H) so every settings screen behaves the same.

system.title: Slider sheet states
system.caption: Five agronomy inputs share one slider sheet, with a color scale and a plain-language 'What this means' panel for each stop.

system.title: Zone details states
system.caption: Zone details covers with, without and resume-in-progress True ET, so every state of an advanced feature is designed rather than implied.
